entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abu al-Hasan 'Ali (c. 997 - 1009) was the ruler of Khwarazm from his accession in 997 until his death around 1009. A member of the Ma'munid dynasty, he was the son of Ma'mun I ibn Muhammad and succeeded his father to the throne.

Ali's reign was marked by significant military campaigns against neighboring territories, including the conquest of parts of modern-day Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. His forces also clashed with those of the Seljuk Turks in Anatolia, leading to a series of bloody battles that shaped the medieval Middle East landscape.

Despite his military successes, Ali's rule was cut short by a devastating plague that ravaged Khwarazm and other parts of Central Asia. The exact cause and impact of this event remain unclear, but it is believed to have weakened Ali's hold on power and paved the way for future conflicts in the region.

The legacy of Abu al-Hasan 'Ali can be seen in the continued rivalry between the Khwarazmian Empire and its neighbors, as well as the ongoing struggle for control over Central Asia's rich trade routes. His reign also highlights the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined medieval politics in the region.
